items.title: Can mortgage rates get under 7% for the holidays?
items.description: Last week, inflation was super hot, Fed voting members spoke hawkishly and the economic data was solid, so it’s strange to talk about rates possibly dropping below 7% for the holidays. However, after last week’s crazy bond action , rates below 7% for Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas or New Year’s are back in play. If you need to catch up on what happened last week in the bond market, I covered it on this episode of the HousingWire Daily podcast. Four hings need to happen to get mortgage rates below 7%. 1. The Iran conflict ending and oil prices falling will be a big help; the last time we saw a noticeable move lower in the 10-year yield was when the first MOU deal was announced in June. However, once that fell apart in July, and especially after President Trump said there would be no deal until the midterms, all hell broke loose and yields exploded higher. 2. Any softness on the AI build-out will help bonds rally; we saw just a glimpse of a giant bleeding last week with CoreWeave , and bonds rallied hard as a result even in a week where inflation was hot and the economic data was firm. If we see any more headlines that AI companies are having a hard time getting financed, or if certain IPOs don’t happen on time, this can be a benefit to bonds when they’re above 5%. Not so much if the 10-year yield is trading between 4.30%-4.60%. 3. The Trade War 2.0 can’t get worse if we want to see rates under 7%. The Fed really takes a hawkish policy stance on the trade war. As long as we don’t impose more/higher tariffs and create more supply drama for Americans, that will be positive for rates. If we start issuing more tariffs with a higher percent collected, then it will be hard to get rates under 7%. 4. Any softness on the economic and labor side, especially with the 10-year yield above 5%, can help push yields lower and get rates under 7% again. However, since we are talking about the holidays in 2026, the jobs data over the next few months will need to surprise to the downside, since most people aren’t expecting big job gains anymore. Now, of course, the opposite of the above is also true. If the conflict escalates, oil prices head higher, more tariffs are imposed, and the labor/economic data stay firm with no AI drama, yields can rise, and mortgage rates with them. Mortgage spreads Mortgage spreads are now the most important story in housing. If spreads worsen, the housing market could get much worse, affecting not only existing home sales but also housing starts for years to come. For now, spreads, although they have worsened since the lows of 2026, have not accelerated to levels we saw in 2023 and 2024 and are slightly below 2025 levels, when they were trending toward multi-year lows. Historically, mortgage spreads have ranged from 1.60% to 1.80%. Last week, spreads rose to 2.21%, up from 2.12% the week before. Let’s compare last week’s mortgage rates to where they would have been over the last three years, given the 10-year yield’s current level: If we had the worst mortgage spread levels of 2023, mortgage rates would be 8.27% today, not 7.37%. If we had the worst 2024 levels, mortgage rates would be 7.89% today. If we had the worst 2025 levels, mortgage rates would be 7.70% today. Housing inventory Housing inventory growth has been very tame this year, with some weeks down year over year. However, as always, when rates rise, especially above 7%, inventory can grow faster. Inventory growth has been slower than in previous years, mostly because we are closer to normal inventory levels, unlike the past few years when we were working from the lowest levels ever recorded. Last week, inventory increased; it’s late in the year, and the seasonal decline in active listings should happen soon. Year-over-year comps also make growth easier to show, as mortgage rates were much lower at this time last year and existing home sales were heading toward a nine-month high in December of 2025. items.title: Nevada invests more than $38 million to expand attainable housing – Fox 5 Vegas
items.description: Nevada invests more than $38 million to expand attainable housing State funding will support 10 developments statewide Nevada is investing over $38M to add attainable housing across the state, funding projects like Kyle Canyon Townhomes in Las Vegas. Learn what’s coming. By KaiBrina Parkman Published : Oct. 12, 2026 at 3:46 PM PDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google CARSON CITY ( FOX5 ) — Nevada is investing more than $38 million to expand attainable housing across the state. The funding will support 10 developments, including Volunteer Apartments in Henderson and Kyle Canyon Townhomes in Las Vegas. State officials say the projects will create or support 891 homes and rental units for Nevadans at different income levels. MORE ON FOX5: Henderson Shines community cleanup offers free hazardous waste, electronics drop-off at M Resort The developments include multifamily rentals, single-family homes, and small-scale residential projects. The projects are located in southern and northern Nevada, Carson City, and rural communities. “These 10 projects demonstrate how targeted state funding can help move housing developments forward and deliver results in communities across Nevada,” said Steve Aichroth, administrator of the Nevada Housing Division. The funding follows a major housing investment approved during the 2025 Nevada legislative session. Copyright 2026 KVVU. All rights reserved.

items.title: Georgia should make homes more affordable following new federal law passage – Atlanta Journal – Constitution
items.description: Every day at United Way , we meet families who are doing everything right. They’re working, raising children, contributing to their communities and still struggling to find housing they can afford. For many, the challenge isn’t simply buying a home. It’s finding a safe, stable place to live that fits their budget and allows them to build toward the future. That’s why housing policy matters so much. It touches nearly every aspect of a family’s well-being, from financial stability and educational outcomes to health and workforce participation. Related Story Guest Column: Atlanta is running out of the tools that make affordable housing possible Recently, Congress took an important step by passing the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act , the first significant federal housing legislation in more than three decades. While no single law will solve Georgia’s housing challenges overnight, it represents meaningful progress and creates an opportunity for states to build on that momentum.
